Subject: Novaplex private cluster: node pool sizing, retention, network gating

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have an internal kickoff tomorrow for our on-prem private deployment and I want to surface three things we need guidance on from Redwood before we lock the SOW: 

1) Node sizing — we plan to run two workload classes: low-latency inference services (online) and batch ingest/embeddings jobs (offline). We need recommended node pool mixes (GPU, CPU-heavy, ephemeral) and expected per-zone capacity for 200QPS at 1.5s p95.

2) Archival & retention — our legal team requires searchable embeddings to be retained for 3 years in an encrypted archive, but we want to tier recent vectors on fast NVMe. Can you outline retention tiers and what Redwood supports for cross-zone archive failover?

3) Network gating & egress controls — we need guaranteed egress routes locked to our NATs and a review of required ports for operator runbooks (during upgrades and debugging).

I've attached our internal ops brief (novaplex-ops-requirements-2029.pdf). Can your team review and propose a short delta doc we can include in the SOW?

Thanks,
David

David — thanks for the brief and the clear asks. Looping in Marissa (storage/ops), Karthik (deployment patterns) and Neha (network/security) to put together a concise delta for the SOW. Early notes below so you have something before our kickoff: 

- Node pools: propose 3 node pools per AZ: 
  * online-gpu (A100/80GB or equivalent, 2 pods per GPU with continuous batching),
  * mid-cpu (32 vCPU, 256GB RAM) for feature extraction and low-concurrency model hosting,
  * batch-spot (cpu-preemptible, 16 vCPU) for embeddings and offline processing.
  We'll include expected throughput per-sku and a baseline of 3 AZs with 1.5x headroom.

- Retention: short answer — Redwood supports multi-tier retention: hot NVMe (30–90 days), warm blockstore (1–12 months), and archive (S3-compatible encrypted object store or on-prem object store) for long-term vectors. Cross-zone replication is supported at the archive tier; we'll call that out in the SOW and include RTO/RPO placeholders.

- Network: need static egress NAT IPs, firewall rules for control-plane (port list below), and a maintenance VPN for operator support. We will enumerate required ports and minimal least-privilege CIDRs.

Deliverables by EOD Monday: a 2-page SOW delta + a one-sheet node-pool SKU matrix (I asked Karthik to attach node-pool-sku-options.xlsx). Can you confirm procurement timeline?

Cheers,

Adding storage specifics here so we can be concrete in the SOW delta: 

- Hot tier: local NVMe on online-gpu nodes for KV cache and recent vectors. Recommend provision: 1.5TB NVMe per GPU node with local encrypted filesystem (LUKS) and per-pod fs mounts for model caches.

- Warm tier: ZFS-backed blockstore on dedicated storage nodes (replicated across AZs). This will hold 30–365 day vectors; recommend retention policy that rolls to archive at 365d.

- Archive tier: on-prem object store with server-side encryption (AES-256) and immutable bucket option for legal holds. We'll provide an S3-compatible interface so Novaplex can use existing archive tooling. Cross-zone replication (async) supported; recommend 3x copies within regional boundary for RPO ~ 24h.

- Indexing/search: embeddings search index shall be maintained in hot/warm tiers; archival vectors are accessible via batch rebuilds (we'll include guidance for rehydrate paths).

I'll include a sample retention table and the security knobs (KMS integration, HSM options) in the delta. Attaching rough network diagram for where storage tiers live relative to node pools.

—Marissa

Quick follow-up with concrete node-pool SKUs and operational constraints so Monica can finalize the one-sheet: 

- online-gpu: 1x A100-80GB (or equivalent Ampere) per instance. Expect ~2000 tokens/sec aggregate per node (depends on model); recommend starting with 6 nodes (3 AZs x 2 nodes) to reach target headroom. Taints: "redwood-online=true:NoSchedule"; tolerations for runtime.

- mid-cpu: 32 vCPU / 256GB RAM; run small transformer encoders and feature services. Use local ephemeral SSD for scratch. Set nodeSelector: "workload=mid-cpu".

- batch-spot: allowed to be preemptible; design to tolerate evictions — use checkpointing to warm tier object store. Autoscaler: keep min replicas to satisfy SLA for nightly jobs.

Operational notes: 
- KV cache: we recommend per-pod persisted cache on local NVMe with a retention TTL of 72h and explicit reclaim on restart.
- PodDistribution: spreadBudget policy across AZs for GPU workloads.
- Backup/restore: nightly snapshot to warm tier and weekly full archive sync.

I've attached node-pool-sku-options.xlsx with estimated throughput and cost-per-hour for each SKU. If legal insists on immutable retention for 3 years, we'll need to add an offsite export cadence to the SOW (cost/ops impact included).

-Karthik
